However, several claims are wrong or loosely supported, and the example claims do not match the narrative.","problems":["Headline says 99215 is above expectation \"at every complexity level\", but the card gives only the provider's own 99215 share by band against the all-provider share. It has no risk-adjusted expectation per band.","The rationale says the 99215 share runs \"roughly two to three times the all-provider rate in every band\". The ratios are about 2.1, 2.6, 2.5, 2.6, 1.9 and 1.4. The 4 and 5+ bands fall below two times, so the claim is overstated.","The \"9% for the comparison providers\" figure is the all-provider 99215 below-billed rate (0.087) from the card, which is plausible. The \"99213 and 99214 in line with peers\" claim rests on 0 of 4 and 1 of 21 documented claims, which is very thin and not caveated there.","The narrative cites C0214578, C0214627, C0215239 and C0214961 as illustrative acute-only visits, but the final Examples list cites C0214258 (back pain, 0 conditions), C0214565 and C0216330 instead. The cited claims do not match the claims discussed, and the only below-billed example is a 99214 claim that is not relevant to 99215.","The summary calls C0215223 and C0215917 low-complexity, but each has one condition, so it is only borderline low-complexity. The phrase \"visits coded only for routine problems\" overreaches for Z09 and R21.","The next steps are generic. They ask for records for a \"larger sample\" without naming the specific claims, even though the rationale names low-complexity claims to request. The second step, re-screen, adds little.","The next-step statement that records exist for only 1% of claims is fine, but the summary does not flag that the 30 documented claims may not be a random sample."]}
